payload.headline: Netflix at 59.41 still below fair value; small adds, support at 56.31

summary.thesis: Netflix is a Grade B business that keeps producing more cash. At 59.41 it trades below most value estimates, but sales growth is slowing and the price trend is still down.
summary.decision: Long-term: keep adding in small, staggered slices below the 64.9 DCF base value. Swing: no trade while the price stays in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: add at 56.81 and 53.74; stop buying above 64.9

payload.happening: Netflix closed at 59.41, up 0.92% on the day. It is still in a downtrend, below its falling 20-day (61.68), 50-day (66.24) and 200-day (79.59) averages. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
payload.business: Several numbers point to a strong business. Trailing free cash flow is 11.4B, up from 9.0B. Operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% over the year (share buybacks). Some numbers do point to a business change: quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago, and the filings flag that the 31% margin is at the top of its 5-year range (17–31%), where margins usually fade. Analysts cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3%, from 0.73 to 0.68. Next year's estimate moved only from 3.81 to 3.77. Other things affect only sentiment or governance. Those are the price trend, put open interest at 2.59 times call open interest (options traders hold more bets on a fall), and 3 new risk headings in the annual report. Debt of 12.7B against cash of 8.2B (net cash -4.4B) is easy to carry with 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. Cash and the balance sheet are not at risk. The risks are the growth rate and how long the margin lasts.

worth.text: To justify today's price, free cash flow has to start growing at about 12.5% a year. That is close to the 15% sales growth of last year and the 15% over 3 years. The DCF (a model that values the company on its future cash flows) gives 38.59 bear, 64.9 base and 77.72 bull. The gap between these comes from the starting growth assumption. At 10% growth the value is 53.74, and at 20% it is 80.23. By its own history, the price-to-sales ratio of 4.9 sits at the 18th percentile of its 5-year range. That ratio puts the price near the 58.94 low end of the 58.94–122.15 history range and below the peer median of 6.8. The stock trades at 16.9 times trailing earnings and 15.8 times next year's. Margins are the main risk. If operating margin falls to 23%, the value is 59.9, about today's price. At 15%, it drops to 39.57.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, around the 12.5% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.

bull: Price-to-sales of 4.9 is below the peer median of 6.8 and sits at the 18th percentile of its own 5-year range.
Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, and operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%.
The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each remaining share owns more of the business.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
This quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3%, and next year's was cut 1.1% in 30 days.
Operating margin is at the top of its 17–31% five-year range. If it falls to 15%, the value is 39.57.

levels.what: Top of the 56.31–56.81 support zone, the next small add. It is below the 59.9 margin-fade value and the 58.94 own-history low.
Value at 10% starting cash-flow growth and the low end of the fair-value range. This is the last planned add before the report.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: At 59.41 the price is below the 64.9 DCF base and close to the 59.9 value even if margins fade to 23%. Estimates are still being trimmed and the trend is down, so adds stay small and staggered.

swing.why: The trend is down and the price is under every falling average. The first resistance at 61.14–61.64 is closer than the 56.31 support, so the upside is smaller than the downside. No trade until a close above 65.08.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report comes after the 2027-01-15 option expiry (which prices an 11.4% move) and before the 2027-02-19 expiry (16.9%). So adds stop at the 53.74 slice before the report, and further buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-19 report shows operating margin heading toward 23%, where value is 59.9, stop adding. Toward 15%, where value is 39.57, the decision moves to avoid.
If next-year EPS estimates drop below the 3.56 low end, the 10%-growth value of 53.74 becomes the ceiling, not the floor.
If the price closes above the 64.56–65.08 resistance, the downtrend has broken, and a swing entry becomes possible with a stop under 61.14.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still add; the price of 59.41 remains below the DCF base (now 64.9) and the 59.9 margin-fade value. A new 56.31–56.81 support zone now gives a level for the next slice.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
